text:
anya: Heads up — after the kernel-selector tweak rolled yesterday we’re seeing tail-latency spikes on long-seq paged-KV workloads (99.9p up ~2.1x). Noticed CPU/GPU imbalance during compaction bursts.

sam: repro or logs? which path is compaction taking — slab vs hybrid?

anya: Repro on staging with lm-7b-longseq. Minimal repro steps: send steady 8k-token requests at ~40 qps. Tail spikes start after ~6min. Attached profiler excerpt below.

matt: can you paste the profiler sample? curious if it’s NVTX or host-side stall.

anya: profiler excerpt (host-side stack samples, aggregated):
```
pager_worker_loop > kv_compactor > slab_free_run > cudaMemcpyAsync > wait_event
pager_worker_loop > kv_compactor > allocate_blocktable > choose_alloc_path(slabs) > try_compact_range
request_worker > kernel_dispatch > flash_attn_v2_launch -> small_streams
```

anya: key observations: compactor wakes frequently (~50-200ms), compaction work often touches many small blocks which causes lots of cross-stream cudaMemcpyAsyncs. GPU kernels run fine but we see queueing on host -> GPU transfer.

lina: interesting. could be hysteresis too low so compaction runs aggressively when throughput temporarily dips. what are current knobs?

anya: current runtime knobs: `kv.compact_threshold=0.35`, `kv.compact_hysteresis_ms=150`, `pager.alloc_strategy=slab`, `pager.max_small_block_pct=0.18`

sam: perf-bot, did CI perf compare before/after selector tweak?

perf-bot: CI results for staging selector-tweak-2026-03-16 -> baseline: 99.9p latency increase 2.08x on lm-7b-longseq (steady QPS). Memory footprint ~+4%. Batch efficiency down ~6%. Full diffs: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/selector-tweak/diff/1809

matt: two hypotheses: 1) selector picks flash_attn_v2 for small micro-batches which increases num kernel launches and host-GPU synchronization; 2) compaction policy interacts with slab allocator producing fragmentation that triggers lots of small memcpy operations.

lina: agree. quick mitigations: bump `kv.compact_hysteresis_ms` to 800-1200ms; temporarily disable compaction on hot path (`kv.compact_disabled=true`) for canary; force `pager.alloc_strategy=hybrid` to avoid immediate slab compaction.

sam: also try forcing kernel variant -> flash_attn_fused or the older flash_attn_v1 for the canary to see kernel impact. we should have a runtime toggle for kernel_override per-model.

anya: I ran a quick canary toggling `kv.compact_hysteresis_ms=1000` + `pager.alloc_strategy=hybrid` on a small shard: 20 min run -> 99.9p down ~1.6x vs patched selector, batch utilization back to baseline. No functional regressions observed.

matt: nice. next: gather GPU-side traces to confirm reduced memcpy spikes. Also run microbenchmarks of flash variants with our typical small-microbatch size distribution (seqs 6k-10k).

lina: will open an RFC for an adaptive-hysteresis: compute hysteresis as a function of observed qps variance and current free-block-frag. baseline rule: hysteresis_ms = clamp(200, 200 + 6*stdev_qps, 3000). Allows calmer compaction when load is bursty.

sam: sounds good. can we also add a telemetry counter for compactions_per_min and avg_compact_block_count so we can set alerting thresholds?

anya: already added lightweight metrics in the canary: `kv.compactions_per_min`, `kv.avg_compact_blocks`, `kv.memcpy_async_per_compact`. will push telemetry to console dashboard.

matt: for the kernel selection side, propose a cheap heuristic: if predicted microbatch_count > 1 and total_seqlen > 4k, prefer fused variant, else flash_v2. Should be a quick patch to selector table.

lina: also note quantized models sometimes change kernel perf crossover point — include model dtype in the selector input.

anya: created an issue and a tiny PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 — includes hysteresis bump, hybrid alloc flag, and selector override flag for canary. Running extended canary now across 3 nodes.

sam: next steps: (1) collect GPU traces and CI microbench results (matt), (2) run adaptive-hysteresis experiment behind feature flag (lina), (3) validate selector heuristic and add model-dtype awareness (matt/sam), (4) monitor telemetry and rollback if anything worse.

lina: tagging @matt for kernel microbench and @anya for canary telemetry. :thumbsup:

anya: I'll post a short follow-up in #eng-releases once canary completes with numbers. thanks all.
